correctness.rationale: The proof follows from invariant-measure identities for \(\log u_i\) and \(\log v\), an exact algebraic reciprocal expansion, and the equilibrium equations. The strict inequality is justified separately: constant predator coordinate on a compact interior invariant support reduces both prey equations to scalar logistic equations, whose only complete compact positive trajectories are equilibria; uniqueness then forces the equilibrium Dirac measure. The equal-fear sign law follows from a positive weighted average and the exact cancellation \(q_1-q_2=(r_1p_2-r_2p_1)/[(p_1+r_1C)(p_2+r_2C)]\). The symbolic checker verifies only the algebraic identities and is not used in place of the analytic strictness proof.

value.rationale: The motivating paper leaves global convergence of the linear shared-predation model as an explicit conjecture. The theorem supplies a finite-amplitude structural constraint on any compact recurrent obstruction: predator mean must rise strictly above the coexistence equilibrium while the weighted prey mean is fixed. In the natural equal-fear case, it further determines which prey mean rises solely from the biological ratios \(r_i/p_i\), independent of oscillation amplitude or invariant-measure shape. This directly addresses how shared predation and fear redistribute long-run mean densities and is more informative than a local or numerical stability check, while making no unsupported claim of global stability.
